title: SSDI initial applications, Apr 2027
question: Social Security Administration State Agency Monthly Workload Data, Field I Receipts (All Initial), SSA month 2027-04, not seasonally adjusted, first print, in thousands, conditional on the 2025 reconciliation law's Medicaid community-engagement compliance deadline taking effect on its statutory schedule with no federal statutory or regulatory delay announced by 2027-03-31
resolutionSource: Social Security Administration State Agency Monthly Workload Data
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first official SSA State Agency Monthly Workload Data CSV print for Date Type MO and Formatted Date 2027-04, summing Field I Receipts (All Initial) across all state-agency and federal-component rows if no national row is provided; convert whole claims to thousands and round to one decimal thousand. Use the first replacement file that adds the 2027-04 period; later replacements or retroactive corrections do not change the resolved value. The resolutionDate is the official within-30-days availability deadline implied by SSA's update rule after the 2027-04 SSA month closes; the operative resolver is the first file replacement that adds 2027-04. The conditional is satisfied only if no federal statutory or regulatory delay of the Medicaid community-engagement compliance deadline is announced by 2027-03-31.
conditionalOn: The 2025 reconciliation law's Medicaid community-engagement compliance deadline takes effect on its statutory schedule, with no federal statutory or regulatory delay announced by 2027-03-31.

reasoning.text: SSA DDS initial disability receipts, April 2027

Framing and exact resolver: this forecast targets SSA State Agency Monthly Workload Data monthly Field I, Receipts (All Initial), for SSA month 2027-04. The variant is not seasonally adjusted DDS/state-agency initial claims, not OASDI beneficiary stocks, not SSI Monthly Statistics, and not final revised annual claims workloads.

reasoning.call: Opened SSA State Agency Monthly Workload Data documentation and data dictionary.
reasoning.result: Fetched official dataset facts: monthly data start in October 2000; the expanded current file has 71 data elements; Field I is Receipts (All Initial); Fields I-M cover All Initial Claims; data are one row per State Code and Date; no summary row is provided; File Version currently has value 2.

reasoning.call: Opened SSA State Agency Monthly Workload Data timing and update-policy documentation.
reasoning.result: Fetched timing evidence: SSA counts monthly work in weekly increments, an SSA month normally ends on the last Friday of the month, the Date field maps to SSA time periods, and the dataset is updated with a new time period within 30 days of the close of the prior time period; April 2027's last Friday is 2027-04-30, so the official within-30-days by-date is 2027-05-30.

reasoning.result: Fetched fiscal year 2024 claims workloads: Disability Insurance claims received total 2,260.6 thousand, worker 2,145.9 thousand, family members and survivors 114.7 thousand; SSI claims received total 1,683.2 thousand, aged 214.1 thousand, blind or disabled 1,469.1 thousand.

reasoning.text: Base rate/reference class: the best fetched official-source class available in this run is recent SSA disability-related claims workload volume. DI total claims received rose from 2,071.7 thousand in FY2022 to 2,111.9 thousand in FY2023 and 2,260.6 thousand in FY2024, equal to simple monthly equivalents of 172.6, 176.0, and 188.4 thousand. The DDS Field I resolver is a monthly flow, so I anchor on a five-week April month rather than a calendar-month stock.

Level, momentum, one-off, and policy mechanism: level starts from the FY2024 monthly-equivalent DI claims volume because the raw SSA-SA-MOWL.csv was identified as the final resolver but was not readable as tabular rows through the draft environment; this makes the annual DI workload prior a downgraded proxy rather than the target-series monthly history. Momentum is upward across FY2022-FY2024; the one-off calendar effect is that April 2027 normally spans five SSA weekly closes; the conditional Medicaid community-engagement mechanism adds a judgmental, scenario-weighted filing-pressure adjustment, but I reduce it because the draft did not fetch a direct eligibility-channeling analog.

Prior/update/interval: persistence prior = FY2024 DI claims received monthly equivalent 2,260.6/12 = 188.4 thousand; historical sample = fetched FY2022-FY2024 DI monthly equivalents converted to five-week SSA-month analogs using 5/(52/12)=1.1538, giving 199.2, 203.1, and 217.4 thousand; adjustment components = +10.0 thousand for partial continuation of the FY2022-FY2024 upward trend into 2027, +6.0 thousand for the conditional Medicaid community-engagement deadline pull-forward/channeling mechanism, and +0.0 for rounding, giving point 217.4 + 10.0 + 6.0 = 233.4 thousand. Interval method uses the values themselves for this flow proxy: sigma = 9.6 thousand across the three five-week analogs, so 1.28*sigma = 12.3 thousand. I widen to a judgmental 40.0 thousand half-width, beyond 1.75x, because the fetched annual DI workload anchors are not the exact monthly DDS Field I target series and the conditional policy mechanism could shift filings around April 2027; final implied bounds are 233.4 +/- 40.0 = 193.4 to 273.4 thousand.

Counter-considerations: upside risk is a larger Medicaid work-requirement response, outreach by advocates, or SSA/DDS intake catch-up that would land above the interval if April 2027 exceeds 273.4 thousand. Downside risk under the stated condition is weak take-up, limited awareness of disability pathways, administrative friction, or filings shifted outside April; the outcome would land below the interval if receipts are under 193.4 thousand. An outside the interval high print would most likely require a broad policy-driven filing surge rather than normal trend.

Review disposition: accepted the critiques to clarify that annual DI workload values are a proxy rather than monthly Field I history, reduce the Medicaid policy adjustment from +12.0 to +6.0 thousand, widen and label the interval as judgmental, remove federal delay as a conditional downside tail, and clarify that 2027-05-30 is the SSA update-rule availability deadline while first replacement file remains the resolver.

findings.summary: The prior is built from FY annual DI claims equivalents rather than the target monthly SSA State Agency Monthly Workload Field I series, even though the resolver CSV is cited.
findings.actionRequested: Use or explicitly tabulate the actual SSA-SA-MOWL Field I monthly history for comparable Aprils and/or five-week SSA months; if the CSV truly cannot be parsed, state that as a limitation and downgrade the model prior rather than treating annual DI totals as the main prior.

findings.summary: The interval is based on only three annual-derived five-week analogs and then widened judgmentally, not on realized monthly target-series volatility.
findings.actionRequested: Derive the half-width from realized variation in the monthly Field I target series, such as comparable April errors, five-week-month dispersion, or a simple time-series residual distribution; otherwise explicitly label the interval as judgmental and justify the 30k width.

findings.summary: The +12k Medicaid community-engagement adjustment is material but not supported by cited evidence on eligibility-channeling, affected population, or historical policy analogs.
findings.actionRequested: Add a compact evidentiary bridge for the policy adjustment, or reduce/reframe it as a judgmental scenario-weighted adjustment with stated uncertainty.

findings.summary: A federal delay is listed as a downside risk, but the forecast is conditional on no federal statutory or regulatory delay announced by 2027-03-31.
findings.actionRequested: Remove delay as an outcome tail under the conditional forecast and replace it with conditional-consistent downside scenarios, such as weak take-up, administrative friction, or filings shifted outside April 2027.

findings.summary: The resolution date is justified as 2027-05-30 from the within-30-days rule, but that may be a deadline rather than the actual first-print date.
findings.actionRequested: Clarify that 2027-05-30 is the resolution deadline/expected availability date under the SSA update rule, and keep the first replacement file adding 2027-04 as the operative first-print rule.

findings.summary: Show the implied prior and final bounds in one short final paragraph so the JSON point and interval are easy to audit.
Distinguish DI annual claims from DDS Field I all-initial receipts wherever both are discussed, since they are not necessarily the same measurement surface.
